newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Super-Sol sees 15 pct sales rise.
newsitem.headline: Super-Sol sees 15 pct sales rise.

text.p: Israel's Super-Sol Ltd expects a 15 percent sales increase after it completed its acquisition of the supermarket business of retailer Shekem Ltd on Sunday, a Super-Sol executive said.
The commissioner for restrictive business practices approved the deal on Friday while imposing certain restrictions on Super-Sol, which already controls one-third of the country's supermarket sales.

"We expect this to increase our sales by 15 percent over projections for this year," Yaacov Ginzburg, Super-Sol's vice president for marketing and purchasing, told Reuters. He would not say what projected sales in shekel terms would be for the year.
He said Super-Sol paid 250 million shekels plus the value of the merchandise in stock for Shekem's 30 stores. As of Sunday, the stores were operating under Super-Sol's various trade names.

Shekem, which is controlled by Elco Holdings Ltd, had said it sold the supermarket chain as part of a reorganisation. The overhaul includes cutting expenses and giving its department stores -- the company's main business -- a more fashionable image.
Shekem has experienced chronic losses. In the first nine months of 1996, it reported a 9.6 million shekel loss on revenues of 854.5 million shekels.

Yoram Turbowicz, the commissioner for restrictive business practices, conditioned his approval of the deal on Super-Sol's honouring contracts with suppliers and submitting disputes that may arise from the deal to arbitration.
The daily Maariv newspaper said Turbowicz was concerned about allowing Super-Sol to expand its stake in the supermarket industry but approved the deal to save Shekem from heavy losses.
